title: Accelerating P&C Delivery with Developer Assistants from Guidewire
body_text: Home Resources Resources Download Center Guidewire Conversations Podcasts Blog Help and Support Insurance Technology FAQ Blog Blog All Blog Posts Best Practices Careers Customer Viewpoint Developers General Interest Intelligent Experience Partner Perspective Technology Trends Developers Accelerating P&C Delivery with Developer Assistants from Guidewire AI is rapidly reshaping how enterprise software is built, tested, and maintained. Development teams are increasingly adopting an intent-driven model, where developers describe the outcome they want and AI-powered coding tools help generate code, answer questions, automate repetitive tasks, and accelerate software delivery. For Guidewire teams, the opportunity is not just to work faster, but to combine those productivity gains with AI that understands the Guidewire platform, its applications, and its development patterns. In this post, we explore how our domain-specific Guidewire Developer Assistants fit into that picture: why they exist, what they are, the results we’ve seen, how they support day-to-day Guidewire development, connect to your existing AI stack, and where we’re taking them next. Why is There a Need for Guidewire Developer Assistants Senior Guidewire developers bring years of product knowledge, architectural understanding, and development experience to every change they make. They understand the code in its broader application context, including how Gosu, product models, effective-dating rules, integration patterns, and UX conventions work together within Guidewire. They know where the critical business logic lives, which patterns are cloud-friendly, and which anti-patterns create long-term risk. That expertise is incredibly valuable, but it doesn’t automatically scale as organizations take on more projects, more teams, and more frequent cloud releases. A Guidewire-native layer makes that deep platform context easier for teams to access and apply in their everyday development work. It brings the expertise and patterns of these experienced Guidewire developers directly into development workflows, helping teams move faster while staying aligned with platform best practices. The Developer Assistants for Gosu, Integrations, and Jutro, now Generally Available (GA) with the Qusar release , provide this Guidewire-native layer, bringing domain-specific context directly into the tools developers use every day. What Being Guidewire‑Native Really Means and What We’ve Seen in Practice So what does it actually mean for a Developer Assistant to be “Guidewire-native”? It means each assistant is designed to operate with the context and awareness needed to support the relevant Guidewire development workflows. A Developer Assistant is an AI coding companion that turns a developer’s intent into concrete, platform-safe code. Four design choices make that possible: Purpose-built for InsuranceSuite , with deep understanding of code syntax, Page Configuration Format (PCF) structures, Guidewire Cloud APIs, and best practices Grounded in Guidewire’s internal documentation , including cookbooks and curated embeddings, rather than just publicly available web data Version-aware , providing guidances aligned with the Guidewire cloud release and project setup in use Delivered as part of your Guidewire toolkit through Model Context Protocol (MCP) , rather than a one‑off chatbot Those design choices aren’t just architectural nice-to-haves; they show up clearly in the results. In our internal experiments, we took the same AI coding tool and ran a suite of 33 Gosu tasks twice, once with the Developer Assistant connected via MCP and once without. Without the Developer Assistant, the AI tool failed all 33 tests and, in one instance, produced code that compiled successfully but failed to start the server because it violated a Guidewire-specific rule. With the Developer Assistant for Gosu connected, it passed all 33 tests and produced clean, Guidewire-compliant code that was ready for review. Additionally, the Developer Assistant for Gosu completed tasks 41% faster by pulling the correct Guidewire patterns from cookbooks in a single step instead of relying on trial and error. Early Access customers and partners have also reported similar reductions in development effort. How Guidewire Developer Assistants Fit in Your Daily Workflow Here are three real Guidewire workflows that show how an AI coding tool, such as Claude Code in our demos, and Developer Assistants work together to streamline multi-step Guidewire tasks into a single intent: i. Understanding and Refactoring Gosu Code Developer Assistant: Gosu In the Gosu demo, the starting point is a long, unfamiliar ClaimCenter class that would normally require a senior developer to modify safely. With the Developer Assistant for Gosu, the developer provides a single prompt describing the new search field needed. Instead of manually stitching together entity, configuration, display key, and PCF updates, a cohesive set of changes proposed by the assistant is reviewed. In practice, this turns complex changes that normally require a senior developer into reviewable proposals that more of the team can safely progress. ii. Building Resilient Integration Gateway Flows Developer Assistant: Integrations In the Integrations demo, the Developer Assistant for Integrations builds an Integration Gateway route that sends open claims to an external fraud scoring system. The Developer Assistant, with access to Integration Gateway knowledge and documentation, generates a starting route. The route is then pushed further with multi-step prompts, generating Java classes from an API file, creating mapping functions, and modifying the existing route. This makes it faster to stand up new, resilient routes without inventing unsupported patterns that create future upgrade or maintenance risk. iii. Designing Jutro-Idiomatic Digital Experiences Developer Assistant: Jutro In the Jutro demo, the Developer Assistant for Jutro helps build a functional personal auto quote experience starting from a blank template. The assistant has access to Jutro development skills, SDK guides, and UX rules so that the generated code uses the right design system components and entity fields. The result is a functional app that feels native to the Jutro Digital Platform, with code, layout, and UX choices aligned to its recommended patterns and practices. How Open Platform Connectivity Brings Guidewire Developer Assistants to Your AI Ecosystem Most of the insurers we work with aren’t starting from zero on AI. You may already have standardized on a primary AI coding assistant, such as Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, or Amazon Kiro. You want Guidewire capabilities to plug into the AI stack you already have. This is exactly what our MCP-based Developer Assistants are designed to support in an open, tool-agnostic way. At a high level, each Developer Assistant is exposed as an MCP server. Existing MCP-aware tools and agentic environments can treat these as “Guidewire tools” that can be invoked whenever a workflow touches Guidewire code, configuration or APIs. This open design delivers three practical benefits: Primary AI environment stays the same - Developers continue working in the tools they already use, which routes Guidewire sub-tasks directly to the relevant Developer Assistant Governance remains centralized in one AI stack - You continue to control models, logging, and guardrails, while Guidewire provides safe, version-aware tools that plug into that environment No need to build a separate Guidewire knowledge layer - Instead of hand-maintaining prompts and retrieval over Guidewire documentation, teams rely on assistants that are maintained and updated by Guidewire In short, you bring the AI foundation that fits your enterprise. We make it Guidewire-aware by plugging in Developer Assistants via MCP. What’s Next for Guidewire Developer Assistants With the Qusar release, we're expanding our AI assistant capabilities to serve more personas across the platform. The new Developer Assistant for Functions, Product Design Assistant for APD, and Data Curation Assistant for Data Studio are all available in Early Access (EA). This means more of your product design, configuration, and curation work can benefit from the same velocity gains you see today with Gosu, Integrations, and Jutro Developer Assistants. Our direction is toward a future where development feels less like assembling individual tools and more like expressing intent. Developers describe the outcome they want, and a fabric of MCP-connected, platform-aware capabilities interprets that intent, breaks down the required work, and proposes a coherent set of changes. For IT leaders, the destination is clear. You want your teams focused on solving the insurance problems that matter, rather than memorizing every nuance of the Guidewire stack. With our open platform MCP-connected Developer Assistants, we handle the domain-specific complexities so your teams can stay focused on delivering better outcomes for your business and policyholders. title: The Final Chapter Begins: Discover Timber Trails at Snoqualmie Ridge
body_text: The Final Chapter Begins: Discover Timber Trails at Snoqualmie Ridge Tri Pointe Homes Washington • August 3, 2026 Share this article Nestled within the breathtaking beauty of Snoqualmie Ridge, Timber Trails offers a rare opportunity to experience a refined Pacific Northwest lifestyle where modern elegance meets effortless comfort. Surrounded by sweeping mountain vistas and just minutes from the iconic Snoqualmie Falls, this intimate enclave invites homeowners into a world where outdoor adventure and small-town charm coexist beautifully. More than just a new neighborhood, Timber Trails represents something far more significant-it is the final opportunity for new construction within the celebrated Snoqualmie Ridge community, marking the closing chapter of one of the Eastside’s most influential planned communities. For over two decades, Snoqualmie Ridge has set the standard for connected living, blending thoughtfully designed homes with parks, trails, schools, and retail. Now, with the debut of Timber Trails, Tri Pointe Homes® introduces a limited collection of just 46 homes, an exclusive chance to be part of a legacy that has shaped how people live in the Pacific Northwest. Elevated Living, Designed for Today Timber Trails features a collection of three-story townhomes and paired homes designed for the way people live today, open, connected, and effortlessly functional. With floorplans ranging from approximately 1,900 to 3,100 square feet, these homes offer three to four bedrooms, expansive great rooms, and seamless indoor-outdoor living spaces ideal for entertaining or unwinding. Homebuyers can choose from to-be-built opportunities , allowing for personalization through Tri Pointe’s curated design studio, or move-in ready homes that reflect the most popular design selections, each thoughtfully inspired by the model homes and the natural beauty of the surrounding Pacific Northwest. Design That Inspires: Two Model Homes With Interiors by Bobby Berk At the heart of Timber Trails are two stunning model homes with interiors brought to life by design expert, Emmy-winning TV host, and author Bobby Berk . Known for his ability to create deeply personal, functional, and beautiful spaces, Berk’s designs at Timber Trails capture both the spirit of the region and the essence of modern living. Plan 1: Alpine Modern A seamless blend of luxury and nature, Alpine Modern celebrates organic materials and contemporary design. Rustic woods, stone accents, and warm plank flooring create an inviting atmosphere anchored by a striking stone fireplace. Expansive windows frame tranquil scenery, bringing the outdoors in. Inside, modern elegance meets natural texture—plush neutral furnishings, reclaimed wood elements, and refined metal finishes create a layered, sophisticated look with rustic charm. The open kitchen features chef-inspired appliances and a minimalist aesthetic, while spa-like bathrooms offer serene retreats with natural wood and stone finishes. Every detail is intentionally designed to create harmony between home and nature. Plan 2: Nordic Nest Inspired by alpine surroundings, Nordic Nest is a cozy, design-forward retreat rooted in Scandinavian simplicity. Warm oak tones flow throughout the home, complemented by soft textiles and a rich yet calming palette of ochre, burgundy, and evergreen. This model embraces comfort and connection, an open-concept layout featuring see through fireplace connecting the outdoor living to interior comforts. Whether enjoying a quiet evening indoors or taking in sunsets from the deck, Nordic Nest offers a sense of calm and belonging, designed for slowing down and savoring each moment. A Premium Lifestyle, Rooted in Place Timber Trails reflects Tri Pointe Homes’ commitment to creating not just homes, but elevated lifestyle experiences . Every residence is designed with intention, blending architectural sophistication, innovative design, and a deep respect for the surrounding environment. Here, homeowners enjoy: Immediate access to miles of trails, parks, and preserved open space Proximity to major employment hubs via I-90 A vibrant, established community with schools, retail, and recreation Homes that reflect both timeless design and modern functionality As opportunities for large-scale communities on the Eastside become increasingly rare, Timber Trails stands apart, not only for its design and location, but for what it represents: the last chance to own a brand-new home in Snoqualmie Ridge . Your Place in the Legacy Timber Trails is more than a new community, it’s a meaningful milestone. A culmination of decades of thoughtful planning, design excellence, and community building. Whether you’re drawn to the personalization of a to-be-built home or the convenience of a move-in ready residence inspired by Bobby Berk’s vision, Timber Trails offers a unique opportunity to step into a lifestyle defined by beauty, connection, and enduring value. The final chapter of Snoqualmie Ridge is here. The question is - will you be part of it? To learn more about Tri Pointe's newest community in Snoqualmie Ridge browse through the Timber Trails community and contact our New Home Specialist to schedule a tour today. title: Cognyte to Showcase Financial Crimes Investigation Technology at IAFCI International Conference
summary: The company will feature its latest technology innovations, including NEXYTE, Cognyte's AI-powered decision intelligence platform at the 2026 International Association of Financial Crimes Investigators (IAFCI) International Conference.
body_text: HERZLIYA, Israel, August 11, 2026 – Cognyte Software Ltd . (NASDAQ: CGNT) (“Cognyte”), a global leader in software-driven technology for investigative analytics, today announced the company will feature its latest technology innovations at the 2026 International Association of Financial Crimes Investigators (IAFCI) International Conference. Cognyte is a Gold Sponsor of the event. WHAT : The IAFCI International Conference is the premier global forum for professionals dedicated to combating financial crimes, hosted annually by the International Association of Financial Crimes Investigators. The event brings together law enforcement, banking, cybersecurity, retail and investigative experts from around the world to share insights, strategies and innovations. WHO : Speak with Cognyte experts and view demonstrations of Cognyte’s latest technology for financial crimes investigations, including NEXYTE, Cognyte’s AI-powered decision intelligence platform. NEXYTE helps investigators fuse data from across the financial ecosystem, automate complex investigative workflows, uncover hidden relationships and turn fragmented information into actionable intelligence faster than ever before. WHEN : August 25-27, 2026, during exhibit hall hours. WHERE : Booth #18 at IAFCI International Conference at the Grand Hyatt Nashville in Nashville, Tennessee. WHY : Financial crime investigations are becoming increasingly complex and data intensive. Traditional investigative approaches create information silos that limit visibility, slow decision-making and make it more difficult to identify sophisticated criminal networks. Domain-specific AI and financial open-source intelligence (OSINT) are reshaping financial crime investigations, making it easy to seamlessly combine corporate records, beneficial ownership data, sanction and watchlist data, blockchain intelligence and more into a single investigative environment. This capability reveals hidden networks, accelerates investigations and enables faster, more informed decisions. Speaking Session: Breaking Down Silos in Financial Crimes Investigations Wednesday, August 26, 4:10 PM Location: Main Stage (Grand Hall D) Speaker: Daniel Kurz Cognyte Financial Crime Consultant, Daniel Kurz will deliver a presentation at the event, showing how traditional investigations are hindered by siloed data and the blind spots this creates. Modern policy and improved OSINT sharing are driving a shift towards a single, unified intelligence system. The presentation details how an international FIU organization leveraged AI-driven decision intelligence to fuse multiple data sources into a unified environment to accelerate an international money laundering investigation and case resolution. Attendees will gain insights into how decision intelligence enhances collaboration, improves intelligence sharing and enables investigators to identify illicit financial activity with greater speed, accuracy, and confidence. This session is ideal for law enforcement, financial crime investigators, intelligence professionals and compliance leaders seeking to modernize investigative capabilities. About Cognyte Cognyte is a global leader in AI-powered investigative analytics solutions that empower customers with Actionable Intelligence for a Safer World®. Cognyte’s solutions enable law enforcement, national security and military intelligence agencies, as well as other organizations, to navigate an increasingly complex threat landscape. With offerings that leverage advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI) and analytics, Cognyte helps customers make sense of growing volumes of fragmented multi-source data to help identify, assess and mitigate risks across dynamic environments, supporting informed, mission-critical investigations and operations. Hundreds of customers worldwide rely on Cognyte’s intelligence platform to uncover insights and reveal what matters, enabling confident decision-making in high-stakes environments. Learn more at www.cognyte.com ### Media Relations Contact: Michelle Allard McMahon Rainier Communications on behalf of Cognyte Software [email protected]

body_text: Revenue of $4.02 billion, with year-over-year growth led by Data Center and Industrial Operating cash flow of $5.5 billion and free cash flow of $4.9 billion on a trailing twelve-month basis or 40% and 36% of revenue, respectively Returned $1.7 billion to shareholders via dividends and share repurchases in the third quarter WILMINGTON, Mass. , Aug. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Analog Devices, Inc. (Nasdaq: ADI), a global semiconductor leader, today announced financial results for its fiscal third quarter 2026, which ended August 1, 2026. "ADI delivered a strong third quarter, exceeding the midpoint of our revenue, margin, and earnings outlook as we capitalized on broad-based demand," said Vincent Roche, CEO and Chair. "We continue to extend our leadership through a powerful combination of innovation, deep customer collaboration, and manufacturing agility. Our investments in these foundational areas, combined with the trust we have built over decades, provide a unique advantage to create, deliver, and capture value in the AI era – for customers and investors alike." "Demand continued to strengthen across our product portfolio and regions throughout the third quarter, which is reflected in our record fourth quarter outlook" said Richard Puccio, CFO. "We believe our balance of disciplined execution and targeted growth investments will enable us to finish the year strongly and carry that momentum into fiscal 2027." Non-GAAP Financial Information This release includes non-GAAP financial measures that are not in accordance with, nor an alternative to, U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) and may be different from non-GAAP measures presented by other companies. In addition, these non-GAAP measures are not based on any comprehensive set of accounting rules or principles. These non-GAAP measures have material limitations in that they do not reflect all of the amounts associated with the Company's results of operations as determined in accordance with GAAP and should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for, the Company's financial results presented in accordance with GAAP. The Company's use of non-GAAP measures, and the underlying methodology when including or excluding certain items, is not necessarily an indication of the results of operations that may be expected in the future, or that the Company will not, in fact, record such items in future periods. You are cautioned not to place undue reliance on these non-GAAP measures. Reconciliations of these non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP financial measures are provided in the financial tables included in this release. Management uses non-GAAP measures internally to evaluate the Company's operating performance from continuing operations against past periods and to budget and allocate resources in future periods. These non-GAAP measures also assist management in evaluating the Company's core business and trends across different reporting periods on a consistent basis. Management also uses these non-GAAP measures as primary performance measurements when communicating with analysts and investors regarding the Company's earnings results and outlook and believes that the presentation of these non-GAAP measures is useful to investors because it provides investors with the operating results that management uses to manage the Company and enables investors and analysts to evaluate the Company's core business. Management also believes that free cash flow, a non-GAAP liquidity measure, is useful both internally and to investors because it is indicative of the Company's ability to pay dividends, purchase common stock, make investments and fund acquisitions and, in the absence of refinancings, to repay its debt obligations. The non-GAAP financial measures referenced by ADI in this release include: adjusted gross margin, adjusted gross margin percentage, adjusted operating expenses, adjusted operating expenses percentage, adjusted operating income, adjusted operating margin, adjusted nonoperating expense (income), adjusted income before income taxes, adjusted provision for income taxes, adjusted tax rate, adjusted diluted earnings per share (EPS), free cash flow, and free cash flow revenue percentage. Adjusted gross margin is defined as gross margin, determined in accordance with GAAP, excluding: certain acquisition related expenses 1, which are described further below . Adjusted gross margin percentage represents adjusted gross margin divided by revenue. Adjusted operating expenses is defined as operating expenses, determined in accordance with GAAP, excluding: certain acquisition related expenses 1 , acquisition related transaction costs 2 , and special charges, net 3 , which are described further below. Adjusted operating expenses percentage represents adjusted operating expenses divided by revenue. Adjusted operating income is defined as operating income, determined in accordance with GAAP, excluding: acquisition related expenses 1 , acquisition related transaction costs 2 , and special charges, net 3 , which are described further below. Adjusted operating margin represents adjusted operating income divided by revenue. Adjusted nonoperating expense (income) is defined as nonoperating expense (income), determined in accordance with GAAP, excluding: certain acquisition related expenses 1 , which is described further below. Adjusted income before income taxes is defined as income before income taxes, determined in accordance with GAAP, excluding: acquisition related expenses 1 , acquisition related transaction costs 2 , and s pecial charges, net 3 , which are described further below. Adjusted provision for income taxes is defined as provision for income taxes, determined in accordance with GAAP, excluding tax related items 4 , which are described further below. Adjusted tax rate represents adjusted provision for income taxes divided by adjusted income before income taxes. Adjusted diluted EPS is defined as diluted EPS, determined in accordance with GAAP, excluding: acquisition related expenses 1 , acquisition related transaction costs 2 , special charges, net 3 , and tax related items 4 , which are described further below. Free cash flow is defined as net cash provided by operating activities, determined in accordance with GAAP, less additions to property, plant and equipment, net. Free cash flow revenue percentage represents free cash flow divided by revenue. 1 Acquisition Related Expenses : Expenses incurred as a result of current and prior period acquisitions and primarily include expenses associated with the fair value adjustments to debt, property, plant and equipment and amortization of acquisition related intangibles, which include acquired intangibles such as purchased technology and customer relationships. We excluded these costs from our non-GAAP measures because they relate to specific transactions and are not reflective of our ongoing financial performance. 2 Acquisition Related Transaction Costs: Costs directly related to the acquisition of Empower Semiconductor, Inc., including legal, accounting and other professional fees as well as integration-related costs. We exclude these costs from our non-GAAP measures because they relate to a specific transaction and are not reflective of our ongoing financial performance. 3 Special Charges, Net : Expenses, net, incurred in connection with facility closures, consolidation of manufacturing facilities, severance, other accelerated stock-based compensation expense and other cost reduction efforts or reorganizational initiatives. We excluded these expenses from our non-GAAP measures because apart from ongoing expense savings as a result of such items, these expenses have no direct correlation to the operation of our business in the future. 4 Tax Related Items: Income tax effect of the non-GAAP items discussed above. We excluded the income tax effect of these tax related items from our non-GAAP measures because they are not associated with the tax expense on our current operating results. title: How to Build a Personal Kanban Board for Life Admin Tasks
summary: Lighten your life admin with a personal Kanban: visualize tasks, tackle them one by one, and feel empowered and organized.
body_text: Why a personal Kanban board makes life admin lighter Bills, renewals, and forms pile up faster than dishes. A personal Kanban makes that pile visible and finite. You see work. You finish work. You feel in control. Kanban rests on two simple rules. Visualize every task . Limit how many you tackle at once . These rules cut mental load and reduce switching. What counts as “life admin” on your board Renewals: license, passport, insurance, subscriptions. Household: repairs, returns, warranties, decluttering. Money: claims, reimbursements, disputes, savings tasks. Health: appointments, prescriptions, screenings. Identity: change of address, voter registration, passwords. Kanban turns “I should do this” into “This is next.” Set up a three‑column personal Kanban for life admin in 10 minutes Keep setup lean. You can grow it later. Start with three columns: Backlog → Doing → Done . Add a small Waiting lane if helpful. Create cards for every task. Use clear verbs. Example: “Renew driver’s license online.” Set a Doing limit (your work‑in‑progress, WIP ). Start with 2 . Fewer tasks means faster finishes. Pull one card into Doing . Pull the next only when a slot opens. Move finished cards to Done . Celebrate small wins. They compound. Write cards that actually move Make each card completable in under 60 minutes. If not, split it. Example: “Gather tax forms” and “Submit return.” Add a tiny cue. Time window, energy, or cost. Keep it human, not technical. Sample life admin cards : Replace smoke alarm batteries. Cancel unwanted trial. Dispute a fee. Book eye exam. Switch mobile plan. Keep life admin moving with simple Kanban rituals Rituals keep the board honest. They also take minutes, not hours. Daily three‑minute check Scan Doing . Remove hidden blockers. Pick the next card only if a slot exists. End by marking one tiny win. Momentum matters. Weekly 15‑minute review Clear stale cards. If it lingers, split or drop it. Reorder the Backlog by impact, not guilt. Count completed cards. Note what helped you finish. Work with a short horizon. Try a quarter. This idea pairs well with the 12‑Week Year approach for solo operators . This approach helps you maintain focus and keep your board lean. Define clear Kanban policies so your board stays honest Policies remove guesswork. Write them once. Follow them daily. Entry rule : A card enters Backlog only if you intend to do it. Ready rule : A card moves to Doing only if it fits the Work in Progress ( WIP ) limit. Blocked rule : If you wait on someone, tag the card “Waiting” and date it. Aging rule : If a card ages past seven days in Doing , split or drop it. Done rule : Define “done” clearly. Example: “Policy renewed and confirmation saved.” These rules protect flow. They also protect your attention. Choose a tool for your personal Kanban without overthinking it Any board beats no board. Start physical if you like. Go digital if you prefer portability. All‑in‑one workspaces keep tasks, contacts, and projects together. Consider Routine or Notion. Dedicated boards focus on cards and flow. Consider Trello or KanbanFlow. If you expect your board to grow, read this comparison of all‑in‑one workspaces versus dedicated project tools . It will help you choose once, not twice. You may also explore other visual methods, such as timelines or checklists. Kanban remains the simplest daily driver for life admin. Make your cards crystal‑clear with helpful metadata Metadata should guide action, not create admin overhead. Energy : Low, medium, high. Pick tasks that fit your current energy. Time : 10, 25, or 45 minutes. Short slots still move work. Context : Home, online, phone, in‑person. Pull the right task for the setting. Cost : Free, $, $$, $$$. Prevent surprise expenses. Keep metadata light. If it slows you down, remove it. Use WIP limits that match real life Most people start with a WIP limit of two. Some thrive with three. Stress test your number. Run seven days with your current limit. If nothing finishes, lower the limit by one. If you finish early, raise it by one. Guard the limit like a promise. It is your attention budget. Handle “Waiting on others” without losing momentum Blocked work is any task you cannot move forward because it depends on another person, a response, or an external event. Keep flow anyway. Create a slim Waiting lane. Date every card you park there. Set a reminder rule. Nudge after three business days. Prepare a fallback. Example: escalate or pick an alternative provider. Avoid filling your Doing lane with tasks that are blocked or dependent on others. It obscures how accurately your board reflects current, actionable work. Track only the metrics that help you finish Two numbers tell the story. Throughput : cards done per week. Lead time : start to finish time. If throughput drops, lower WIP or split cards smaller. If lead time spikes, hunt for recurring blockers. Keep a tiny log if you like. A single line per week is enough. Troubleshoot common Kanban pitfalls for life admin Problem : Backlog grows forever. Fix : Add a “Someday” purge every month. Problem : You start many, finish few. Fix : Cut WIP. Halve it for one week. Problem : Vague cards stall. Fix : Rewrite with a clear verb and end state. Problem : Urgent tasks hijack the board. Fix : Create a one‑slot “Expedite” lane. Problem : Household work mixes with work work. Fix : Use separate swimlanes. Run a household or partner board smoothly Shared boards reduce repeat questions and missed tasks. Keep them friendly, not managerial. Agree on a single Work in Progress ( WIP ) limit for shared tasks in the Doing column. Use initials on cards, not job titles. Hold a five‑minute check‑in once a week. Archive finished cards monthly. The board stays light. Stay kind. The goal is progress, not perfection. Scale your personal Kanban when life gets busier When the board feels tight, add structure slowly. Swimlanes : Separate “Home,” “Money,” and “Health.” Classes of service : Mark urgent work with a bright color. Checklists : Add a short list inside a big card. Keep it brief. Templates : Reuse common sequences. Example: “Move homes” or “Car service.” If your world spans clients or side projects, pick a flexible tool. You might need contact views or light CRM features over time. Choose a review horizon that matches real motivation Annual goals often drift. Short windows drive action. Many individuals thrive with a 12‑week lens. Consider aligning your backlog with a quarter. Read how to pick that focus in this resource . Use it to decide what truly belongs on the board now. Where to learn more about simple, practical Kanban Want a concise primer before you start? Skim the Atlassian overview of Kanban basics . Then return and build your board today. FAQ How can a personal Kanban board reduce life admin stress? A personal Kanban board makes tasks visible and manageable, reducing the chaos of life admin. It prevents task overwhelm by limiting how much you're doing at once, resulting in better focus and completion rates. Why is it recommended to use a Work in Progress (WIP) limit on a Kanban board? A WIP limit ensures that you are not overwhelmed with tasks, improving focus and efficiency. Without it, the board can become cluttered, leading to multitasking and decreased productivity. How does Routine support personal Kanban boards? Routine offers an all-in-one platform where you can keep your Kanban board, tasks, and contacts integrated. It streamlines workflow management by keeping everything in one place, especially as your board scales. Are separate lanes advisable for shared household Kanban boards? Yes, separate lanes prevent confusion between differing responsibilities like household tasks versus work-related ones. This organization ensures clearer focus and prevents tasks from being overlooked. What is a common issue with life admin Kanban boards and how can it be resolved? Backlogs can grow indefinitely, leading to a cluttered board that's hard to manage. Combat this by purging your \"Someday\" list each month and re-prioritizing tasks based on current relevance and impact. How can metadata on Kanban cards enhance task management? Metadata such as energy, time, context, and cost provide essential cues for task prioritization and can prevent costly inefficiencies. However, ensure that these cues are simple to avoid becoming burdensome in themselves. What should you do if tasks frequently get blocked? Use a “Waiting” lane to track tasks that rely on external inputs, and nudge follow-ups after a defined period. Keep this list minimal to maintain your board's reflection of active work and to prevent stalling progress. Can a Kanban board become counterproductive without proper maintenance? Absolutely. Without regular reviews and WIP limits, your Kanban board can transform into an unmanageable backlog. Continuous prioritization and updates are key to keeping it effective.

title: Byrna Technologies Appoints Marketing Transformation Leader Nate Secor as Senior Vice President of Brand and Marketing
body_text: Byrna Technologies Appoints Marketing Transformation Leader Nate Secor as Senior Vice President of Brand and Marketing Download as PDF August 10, 2026 8:00am EDT ANDOVER, Mass., Aug. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Byrna Technologies Inc. (“Byrna” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: BYRN) , a personal defense technology company specializing in the development, manufacture, and sale of innovative less-lethal personal security solutions, announced the appointment of Nate Secor as Senior Vice President of Brand and Marketing, effective today, August 10, 2026. Secor will oversee the Company’s brand strategy, consumer acquisition initiatives, agency partnerships, and marketing operations. He will report directly to Byrna CEO Conn Davis. Secor joins Byrna with nearly two decades of experience building consumer brands, driving demand generation, leading marketing transformations, and developing customer-centric growth strategies for globally recognized brands. Throughout his career, he has successfully modernized marketing organizations, launched category-defining products, improved customer acquisition performance, and built scalable marketing systems that connect brand investment directly to business outcomes. Most recently, Secor served as Vice President of Marketing for Indian Motorcycle Company, where he was responsible for global marketing strategy across brand, product marketing, digital marketing, paid media, dealer marketing, and consumer engagement. In that role, he led the brand’s transition to its next chapter as part of an independent company, restructured the marketing organization around an integrated demand-generation model, and developed measurement frameworks that connected marketing activity directly to revenue, loyalty, and market share growth. “Nate is exactly the type of marketing leader we need as Byrna continues building the foundation for its next phase of growth,” said Conn Davis, CEO of Byrna. “We are actively transforming how Byrna builds demand, communicates with consumers, measures marketing effectiveness, and expands into new consumer segments. Nate brings a unique combination of brand-building expertise, performance marketing discipline, and operational rigor that will help us accelerate those initiatives. He will play a critical role in managing our growing ecosystem of agency partners while helping us build a more modern and scalable marketing organization.” Prior to Indian Motorcycle, Secor spent more than 15 years with Polaris Industries in a variety of senior marketing and commercial leadership positions. During his tenure, he managed global marketing organizations across North America, Europe, and Asia, oversaw marketing budgets exceeding $20 million annually, and launched numerous major products across Polaris’ portfolio of enthusiast-driven consumer brands. He helped double annual lead generation while reducing acquisition costs and helped deliver record market share performance across multiple product categories. His expertise building customer acquisition programs across complex distribution networks is directly relevant to Byrna’s efforts to reach new consumer segments while improving marketing efficiency. At Byrna, Secor will help lead the Company’s ongoing marketing transformation, including the development of new audience strategies, enhanced consumer acquisition programs, and improved performance measurement capabilities. His responsibilities will include working closely with Byrna’s brand and creative partner HLK, as well as overseeing the Company’s expanding creator, affiliate, social media, and consumer engagement initiatives. “What stands out immediately about Byrna is the strength of the mission, the passion of the customer base, and the size of the opportunity ahead,” said Secor. “The Company is taking important steps to evolve how it approaches marketing and brand development. I look forward to partnering with Conn, the leadership team, and our agency partners to build deeper consumer connections, strengthen the brand, and create a demand-generation platform capable of supporting Byrna’s next growth phase.” Secor earned his MBA in Marketing and Leadership from Indiana University’s Kelley School of Business and holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Marketing from Indiana University. About Byrna Technologies Inc. Byrna is a personal defense technology company specializing in the development, manufacture, and sale of innovative less-lethal personal security solutions. For more information on the Company, please visit the corporate website here or the Company’s investor relations site here . The Company is the manufacturer of the Byrna® CL, Byrna® LE and Byrna® SD personal security devices, state-of-the-art handheld CO2 powered launchers designed to provide a less-lethal alternative to a firearm for the consumer, private security, and law enforcement markets. title: How Agentforce-Powered AI Security Workflows Accelerate Incident Response
summary: Learn how Salesforce uses Agentforce-powered AI security workflows to accelerate incident response, automate investigations, and improve remediation.
body_text: In our Engineering Energizers Q&A series, we highlight the engineering minds driving innovation across Salesforce. Today, we spotlight Zac Taylor, a software engineering architect on the Trusted Services team. Zac and his team are building Security Center, an Agentforce -powered visibility tool that helps accelerate AI-powered security investigations and remediation workflows. The latest release accelerated engineering velocity by 2–3X while enabling security teams to burrow deeper into telemetry, rapidly chase anomalies across distributed systems, and scale AI-driven security playbooks. Explore how the team expanded Security Center’s AI capabilities from a standalone conversational interface into a stateful investigations platform capable of managing long-running security incidents across multiple telemetry systems, along with how the team addressed the challenge of maintaining accurate, trustworthy AI-driven security responses across non-deterministic LLM workflows. What is your team’s mission in building an AI-powered agent, and how does it extend Security Center’s capabilities for managing security operations? The mission is to enhance Security Center with AI-powered capabilities to help organizations investigate threats, respond to incidents, and strengthen Salesforce-specific security operations. Many organizations already run sophisticated infrastructure security programs, but Salesforce environments introduce unique operational and telemetry challenges that traditional security tooling does not address effectively. With Agentforce acting as a Salesforce-native security analyst, customers can investigate suspicious activity, review relevant telemetry, and receive remediation guidance through natural language instead of manually navigating distributed security tooling and operational dashboards. AI makes it possible to summarize large volumes of telemetry and investigation context into concise, actionable responses, giving organizations greater visibility, stronger layered protection, and more adaptive incident response playbooks across increasingly complex telemetry environments. After Security Center became powered by Agentforce, how did the agent expand its capabilities to support end-to-end security investigations? We first focused on delivering a conversational AI experience where customers could ask questions about security findings and telemetry. Very quickly, it became clear that real incident-response systems require significantly more than a standalone chat interface. Security investigations behave more like long-running operational systems than transient conversations. A single incident can span triage, investigation, escalation, communication, and resolution that span rapidly changing operational game scripts. That pushed the team toward building a broader investigations platform with investigation lifecycle management, remediation tracking, auditability, and visualization tools. The result was investigation-focused workflow hubs and state-management capabilities that allow customers to manage incidents end to end across evolving remediation flows. Conversational AI alone is not sufficient for enterprise-grade incident response across complex telemetry jungle environments with today’s rapidly evolving threat landscape. What made non-deterministic LLM behavior difficult to validate consistently at scale for AI-powered security investigations? LLM-driven systems break traditional deterministic testing because identical prompts can generate different responses across executions. That becomes especially pertinent in security workflows, especially under the high-pressure conditions that often arise during active incidents. To solve this, the team built AI-driven evaluation pipelines where AI systems validate the behavior of other AI systems. Large collections of simulated customer interactions are fed into the agent, and LLM evaluators assess whether responses align with the intended investigative outcome and operational expectations. Critically, those evaluators do not validate exact wording. Instead, they assess whether the response satisfies the intended investigative behavior while remaining accurate and contextually grounded through more adaptive read-and-react evaluation strategies. The impact was significant. AI-generated testing increased throughput by roughly 10–20X while enabling continuous evaluation of new investigation scenarios, prompt variations, and customer interaction patterns that would be impractical to validate manually across traditional telemetry samples, retrieval pipelines, and broader investigation coverage models. What made balancing investigative depth, response accuracy, and trustworthy AI reasoning difficult in real-world security investigations? One of the hardest engineering problems was balancing conversational flexibility with highly precise security reasoning. Security investigations quickly evolve from broad questions into deep operational analysis, where customers may start by asking about suspicious activity, then progressively burrow deeper into specific APIs, telemetry patterns, user actions, or remediation history tied to the investigation. Maintaining coherent reasoning across those workflows is difficult because LLM context windows are finite and investigations often span multiple telemetry systems with large volumes of data. Large investigations can trigger reasoning pocket collapse scenarios where critical operational context falls outside the active context window. Hallucination mitigation became equally important. Inaccurate security investigations can overstate blast radius, generate false positives, or erode operational trust. The team addressed this through careful prompt engineering, structured action routing, controlled data-source selection, and rigorous automated evaluation strategies. Continuous refinement was also necessary because customers frequently interact with Agentforce , using ambiguous language, unexpected terminology, or unforeseen questions. What architectural challenges emerged when combining security telemetry, remediation workflows, and multi-system investigation data? One of the largest architectural challenges was handling the wide array of security signals and telemetry systems across Salesforce. Security investigations can originate from many different internal systems, each with different data models, telemetry formats, remediation workflows, and operational implications. Session hijacking incidents, API anomalies, suspicious user behavior, and other threat categories all carry different remediation requirements and security context. To mitigate this, the team designed extensible investigation data models capable of handling disparate telemetry formats and multiple investigation categories without tightly coupling the architecture to specific threat types. Aggregating telemetry from heterogeneous security systems while staying within LLM context window constraints introduced a separate challenge. Investigation telemetry grows extremely large very quickly, making it impractical to pass raw data directly into the model. The team addressed this by partitioning telemetry into smaller contextual segments and using AI-driven summarization pipelines to compress investigation state into more manageable representations before feeding it into the agent. The broader architecture relied on orchestration layers and retrieval pipelines coordinating workflow state across distributed remediation systems, with strong layered protection schemes capable of handling operational edge pressure while maintaining consistent telemetry coverage. Coordinated workflow handoffs, intelligent fallback paths, adaptive remediation route trees, and increasingly dynamic operational cadence were all required to support active investigations at scale. What challenges still remain in grounding AI security responses with Salesforce-specific remediation and investigation knowledge? We are continuing to improve Salesforce-specific grounding. Current agentic workflows rely heavily on publicly available foundation models. Those models carry some Salesforce security awareness derived from public internet content. However, they do not inherently understand Salesforce-specific remediation logic, security operations workflows, or platform-specific threat models. That gap becomes increasingly important as the agent expands into more advanced remediation planning and autonomous investigation workflows where customers expect highly accurate, Salesforce-specific guidance. To address this, the team is working closely with the Setup Agent organization to build stronger grounding systems capable of injecting curated, Salesforce-owned security knowledge directly into the agent context. The long-term vision is that Security Center helps organizations manage investigations, remediation, and operational decision-making directly inside Salesforce — with battle-tested orchestration patterns, faster incident containment, adaptive defensive postures, and more intelligent investigation reasoning across evolving security environments. body_text: Share this page: Manchester United and Super Group today announced a multi-year partnership that will see Betway become the club’s Principal Partner and Exclusive Global Betting Partner. The agreement, which begins with the 2026/27 season, represents Betway’s biggest football partnership to date. Manchester United join Betway’s market-leading sports sponsorship portfolio, which includes partnerships across top-flight football, F1, international rugby union, cricket, basketball and tennis. The deal will see the Betway logo appear on the training kits of Manchester United’s men’s and women’s teams. The brand will also feature prominently on matchdays at Old Trafford and the Progress with Unity Stadium. Additionally, supporters will have more opportunities to connect with the club through exclusive competitions and once-in-a-lifetime experiences. As part of our commitment to providing an enjoyable and safe gaming experience, our partnership will offer comprehensive safer gambling resources to Manchester United players, staff and fans, including training and guidance on responsible gambling and betting integrity. Neal Menashe, Chief Executive Officer of Super Group, commented: “We are thrilled that our Betway brand will be the Principal Partner and Exclusive Global Betting Partner of one of the world’s biggest football clubs. Manchester United’s global reach, particularly with their massive fanbase across Africa, aligns perfectly with our key markets. The Premier League is the world’s most-watched domestic football competition and provides a powerful platform to connect with fans globally. We’re excited to see the Betway brand showcased at Old Trafford, and beyond, as part of our ongoing presence in English football’s top-flight.” Marc Armstrong, Chief Business Officer at Manchester United, said: “We are delighted to welcome Betway as our Principal Partner. The scale of our exciting new partnership reflects our growth strategy, the enduring global strength and appeal of Manchester United, and our ability to attract leading brands that want to engage with our vast worldwide fanbase. Betway are a world-renowned brand with significant presence across world sport. We look forward to working together to help accelerate their global ambitions and create new opportunities to bring supporters closer to Manchester United.” Watch our partnership kick into action below!

title: 65 mensagens de Dia do Cliente para agradecer e encantar seu público
summary: Confira 65 opções de mensagens de Dia do Cliente para demonstrar gratidão, fortalecer o relacionamento e movimentar suas vendas.
body_text: Manter as portas abertas e as prateleiras girando todos os dias exige um ingrediente fundamental: a confiança de quem escolhe comprar no seu balcão . Agradecer a preferência de quem apoia a sua operação não é apenas um gesto de cortesia, mas uma decisão estratégica de gestão. De acordo com a pesquisa Panorama da Fidelização no Brasil , de 2025, 81,9% dos consumidores brasileiros afirmam que o reconhecimento influencia diretamente a sua fidelidade a uma marca. Nesse cenário, enviar uma mensagem de Dia do Cliente bem planejada ajuda a transformar a data comemorativa em um ponto de contato valioso. Confira a seguir ideias de frases de agradecimento para manter sua marca viva na memória do público e criar oportunidades de vendas. Por que enviar uma mensagem de agradecimento no Dia do Cliente? O Dia do Cliente , celebrado em 15 de setembro, foi criado para valorizar quem movimenta o comércio e manter o relacionamento aquecido em um período do ano que antecede as grandes datas festivas. title: Corsair vs Composio: Best MCP Server Platform for Connecting AI Agents to Apps
summary: Corsair vs Composio: compare MCP support, app integrations, authentication, deployment, open-source flexibility, and pricing to choose the right AI agent integration platform.
body_text: Picking the layer that connects your AI agent to the outside world is one of the few infrastructure decisions that is genuinely hard to reverse once your product is in front of users. Credentials, permissions, and every tool call your agent makes will run through it, so the choice shapes how fast you ship, how much you pay as usage grows, and how much control you keep over your own stack. Two names come up constantly in that search: Corsair, an open source integration layer built around MCP, and Composio, a managed platform with a catalog of more than 1,000 prebuilt app integrations. This guide walks through how each one handles MCP, app access, authentication, deployment, and pricing, so you can see exactly where they overlap and where they pull apart. What Is an MCP Server and How Do Corsair and Composio Use One An MCP server is the piece of infrastructure that exposes a set of tools, actions, and data sources to an AI agent in a standard, predictable format, so the agent can call Gmail, Slack, or a CRM the same way it calls any other tool, without your team writing custom glue code for every provider. It is the layer that turns "the agent knows what it should do" into "the agent can actually go do it." For a closer look at why this matters for your product, our guide on how MCP integration benefits your business breaks down the mechanics in more depth. Corsair builds MCP support directly into its core SDK. When you configure Corsair with a set of plugins such as Notion, Slack, Gmail, or Google Calendar, those tools are exposed to your agent through MCP out of the gate, whether you are running Corsair self hosted or through the hosted Corsair Hub. There is no separate product to buy or configure. It is the same layer whether you are calling it from a typed function in your codebase or letting an agent reach for it directly. Composio treats MCP as its own dedicated product surface, called MCP Gateway. It sits in front of Composio's full toolkit catalog and acts as the bridge between MCP capable agents, such as Claude, Cursor, or Codex, and the more than 1,000 apps Composio already supports. This gives Composio's MCP layer very broad coverage out of the box, but it is one more managed component sitting between your agent and the tools it uses, running entirely on Composio's infrastructure. How Do You Give an AI Agent Access to Thousands of Apps Composio's biggest selling point is sheer breadth. Its toolkit directory spans well over 1,000 apps across categories like developer tools, CRM, marketing and social media, finance, ecommerce, and productivity, all managed centrally and ready to use without writing a connector yourself. If your stack is made up of common, mainstream SaaS tools, that catalog gets an agent talking to most of them almost immediately. Corsair takes a narrower but different approach. It ships with a set of curated, production tested plugins covering the tools most AI products actually need first: Gmail, Slack, Notion, HubSpot, Google Calendar, Stripe, Airtable, Linear, GitHub, PostHog, Resend, Google Sheets, Discord, and Tavily, among others. The difference shows up when the app you need is not on that list. Because Corsair is open source, you can scaffold a new plugin yourself with a single command and ship it, or open a pull request and have your team's addition merged so every other user benefits. Composio's catalog grows on Composio's schedule, through its own team and a request queue. Corsair's catalog grows on your schedule, because you can write the missing piece yourself. How Do You Manage Authentication for AI Agent Tool Calls This is where the two platforms diverge most sharply in philosophy. Composio offers managed authentication across OAuth, API keys, and basic auth for every app in its catalog, with delegated access so an agent can act on a user's behalf without your team building auth flows for each provider. Its enterprise tier adds SOC 2 compliance for teams that need a formal audit trail around how that access is handled. Corsair resolves credentials internally at call time, which means your agent only ever sees method names and results, never raw API keys or tokens. Every integration has a configurable permission mode, and destructive actions can require explicit approval before they run, so a user gets a review prompt instead of a surprise. The more structural difference is where the credentials physically live. On the hosted Corsair Hub, none of your customers' credentials or data are stored on Corsair's side at all. Everything lives in your own database, isolated per tenant, so if Corsair's database were ever compromised, there would be nothing of yours in it to expose. That is a meaningfully different security posture than a platform holding delegated access to your users' accounts on your behalf. Open Source or Managed: Which Is the Better Automation Platform for AI Agents Composio is closed source. You use it as a managed service, and enterprise customers can negotiate VPC or on premises deployment, but the platform itself is not something you can inspect, fork, or run independently outside of that arrangement. Corsair is licensed under Apache 2.0 and fully open source, with more than 5,500 stars on GitHub and an active Discord community contributing plugins and fixes. You can self host the full SDK on your own infrastructure for free, with no per seat pricing and no vendor markup added to the API calls you are already paying the third party provider for. If a specific integration is missing, you are never stuck waiting on someone else's roadmap. We covered this tradeoff in more general terms in our post on open source versus closed source integration tools, which is worth a read if licensing model is a major factor in your decision. How Much Does It Cost to Scale AI Agent Integrations Pricing is where the two platforms behave the most differently as usage grows. Composio prices by volume of tool calls. The free tier includes 20,000 tool calls a month with community support. The next tier is $29 a month for 200,000 calls, and $229 a month covers 2 million calls, with additional calls above each tier's allowance billed per 1,000 at a rate of roughly $0.25 to $0.30. Enterprise pricing is negotiated and adds SOC 2 compliance, custom volume, and VPC or on premises deployment. Corsair prices by team size and infrastructure needs rather than usage. Tool calls are unlimited on every tier, including the free Hobby plan. Hobby is $0 a month, supports up to 3 team members, and includes 50 connections and 100,000 webhook events, with Corsair branding on the consent screen. Pro is $200 a month for unlimited connections, unlimited webhooks, unlimited team members, and custom branding. Enterprise is custom priced for teams with more specific requirements. If you self host instead of using the hosted Hub, there is no charge from Corsair at all beyond whatever you already pay the third party APIs you connect to. You can see the full breakdown on our pricing page . For a product whose agent might make an unpredictable or spiky number of tool calls, a flat plan with unlimited calls is a lot easier to forecast than one where your bill moves in step with usage. Corsair vs Composio at a Glance License Corsair: Open source under Apache 2.0, with the full codebase on GitHub. Composio: Closed source, managed platform. Deployment Corsair: Self host for free on your own infrastructure, or use the hosted Corsair Hub. Composio: Hosted by default, with VPC or on premises available on negotiated enterprise plans. App Integrations Corsair: A curated set of production ready plugins, extensible by anyone through open source contributions. Composio: More than 1,000 prebuilt toolkits across a wide range of categories. MCP Support Corsair: Built into the core SDK by default, no separate product required. Composio: Offered as a dedicated product called MCP Gateway. Authentication and Credentials Corsair: Credentials resolved internally and stored in your own database, never exposed to the agent. Composio: Managed OAuth, API key, and basic auth handled centrally by Composio, with SOC 2 compliance at the enterprise tier. Pricing Model Corsair: Flat monthly plans with unlimited tool calls at every tier, including free. Composio: Usage based pricing metered by tool calls, with per call overage above each tier's allowance. Support Corsair: Discord community on Hobby, Slack on Pro, custom on Enterprise. Composio: Community support on the free tier, email on the entry paid tier, and Slack once usage passes 1,000 calls a month. Which Platform Should You Choose If your priority is getting an agent talking to the widest possible range of mainstream SaaS apps as fast as possible and you are comfortable with a managed, closed source platform and usage based billing, Composio's catalog is built exactly for that. If your priority is owning your integration layer outright, keeping customer credentials inside your own database, and never being blocked by a vendor's roadmap when you need a tool that is not already supported, an open source layer built for that purpose is the better fit. That is the gap Corsair is built to close. As an open source integration layer for AI agents, Corsair connects agents to your tools through MCP, handles credential storage, permission gating, and multi tenant isolation from the start, and lets you self host for free or scale on a flat, predictable plan with unlimited tool calls. Instead of metering every action your agent takes or waiting on someone else to ship the integration you need, you get the plumbing solved once, with the option to open the hood and extend it yourself whenever your product needs something the catalog does not already cover.

title: 8x8 Alternatives: Deep dive into the top cold calling options for 2026
summary: Compare the best 8x8 alternatives for 2026, including Trellus, RingCentral, Nextiva, CloudTalk, Dialpad, and Aircall with pricing and features.
body_text: For years, 8x8 has been one of the most recognizable names in business communications. The company began life as a semiconductor manufacturer back in 1987 before moving into internet telephony around the early 2000s. Since then, it has evolved into a complete business communication platform offering voice, messaging, video conferencing, and enterprise grade contact center software. For large enterprises with hundreds of agents, global offices, and dedicated IT departments, 8x8 continues to be a capable solution. It covers almost every communication requirement a large organization could need. Small and growing sales organizations, however, often have a very different experience. Many outbound sales teams simply want a reliable cloud business phone system that lets representatives make more calls, connect with prospects faster, update CRM records automatically, and coach new hires without managing dozens of enterprise settings. When a platform becomes difficult to configure or expensive to expand, teams naturally begin searching for better options. That explains why searches for 8x8 alternatives have continued to grow throughout 2026. Modern UCaaS platforms now include AI powered coaching, automated note taking, CRM synchronization, predictive dialing, conversation intelligence, and mobile first workspaces as standard features instead of expensive enterprise add ons. Pricing has also become much more transparent, making it easier for growing companies to forecast software costs without lengthy sales negotiations. If your team spends most of its day prospecting instead of managing inbound support queues, there are now several VoIP service providers designed specifically for outbound revenue generation. Also Read: 7 CallTools Alternatives to Demo (And 3 Categories That Weren't Worth the Setup) The 6 Best ConnectAndSell Alternatives We Tested for More Live Conversations 7 Synthflow Alternatives That Offer More Than Voice Synthesis Over the next few sections, you'll see seven excellent alternatives that fit different business sizes and sales workflows. Some prioritize AI coaching. Others focus on international calling, CRM integrations, or predictable pricing. The right platform depends on how your team sells every day. # Software Best For Starting Price Key Strength Main Drawback 1 Nextiva Large sales organizations needing an all-in-one communication platform $23/user/month Complete UCaaS platform with calling, messaging, meetings, CRM, and analytics Advanced AI features require higher-tier plans 2 RingCentral Established businesses with complex communication needs $30/user/month 500+ integrations and enterprise-grade reliability Can feel overly complex for smaller teams 3 Trellus Outbound sales teams focused on pipeline generation $99.99/month Parallel dialing, AI coaching, AI practice calls, LinkedIn workflow Built primarily for outbound sales rather than general business communications 4 CloudTalk Scaling SMB sales and customer support teams $25/user/month Excellent CRM automation and international calling Parallel dialing requires an additional add-on 5 Dialpad Businesses wanting native AI coaching during live calls $15/user/month Real-time AI transcription and coaching Premium support and routing require higher plans 6 Aircall Sales teams using HubSpot or Salesforce $30/user/month Excellent CRM integrations and fast onboarding Minimum three-user requirement 1. Nextiva, Best for Large Sales Teams Looking for an All in One Communication Platform What is Nextiva? Nextiva has spent well over fifteen years building one of the most complete communication ecosystems available for businesses. Rather than positioning itself as just another business phone provider, the company combines voice calling, video meetings, team messaging, SMS conversations, customer management, ticket handling, analytics, and collaboration into one unified workspace. For organizations managing large internal departments, this creates a single environment where sales, customer support, management, and operations communicate without bouncing between multiple applications. Many businesses considering 8x8 alternatives appreciate this simplified experience because everything remains under one subscription instead of stitching together several different software products. Nextiva is particularly popular among United States based organizations that want enterprise level communication features without maintaining complex telecom infrastructure. Its platform supports traditional desk phones, desktop applications, web browsers, and mobile devices, giving employees the freedom to work from nearly anywhere while maintaining a consistent business presence. Why Nextiva Is a Good Alternative to 8x8 There are several reasons companies compare these two platforms. Both provide enterprise grade calling, messaging, and collaboration tools, yet their day to day experience feels noticeably different. Better suited for domestic North American businesses 8x8 serves organizations operating across more than one hundred countries. Global coverage sounds impressive, although many regional businesses never use most of those capabilities. Nextiva keeps its attention largely on the United States and parts of Canada. Companies serving local or national markets often find the platform simpler because it removes layers of international administration that many teams never need. Easier pricing to understand Software budgeting becomes much easier when pricing is published openly. Nextiva clearly lists its subscription tiers, making it simple for finance teams to estimate annual software expenses before speaking with sales representatives. 8x8 often requires discussions with account executives before businesses receive complete pricing information for advanced plans. This creates extra work during software evaluations. Complete communication suite under one roof Companies searching for a full business communication platform frequently prefer having voice, SMS, meetings, collaboration, and customer conversations available inside one application. Nextiva delivers all of these services together, making it attractive for businesses trying to reduce software sprawl. Positive customer satisfaction User reviews remain an important consideration when comparing cloud business phone system providers. Nextiva consistently receives higher customer satisfaction scores across major software review websites, particularly around reliability and onboarding. Several 8x8 reviewers mention slower support experiences and inconsistent product knowledge from service representatives, concerns that naturally encourage businesses to evaluate other UCaaS platforms. Things to keep in mind No platform is perfect. AI powered capabilities become available only on higher subscription levels, making advanced automation significantly more expensive. Some features that competitors include within entry level plans also require upgrading to more expensive Nextiva subscriptions. For larger organizations wanting one communication hub without the heavier contact center emphasis found inside 8x8, Nextiva remains a compelling option. Nextiva Pricing Nextiva currently offers three primary subscription tiers. Core, $23 per user each month This entry plan includes business calling, SMS messaging, video meetings, team collaboration, and standard routing capabilities. It covers the communication essentials for many growing businesses. Engage, $50 per user each month This plan introduces advanced reporting, CRM integrations, web chat functionality, and toll free numbers. Sales organizations looking for richer customer insights usually begin here. Power Suite CX, $75 per user each month Designed for larger customer facing teams, this package includes AI generated summaries, intelligent routing, conversation analytics, and advanced reporting capabilities that suit high volume contact center software deployments. 2. RingCentral, Best for Established Businesses That Need a Mature Communication Ecosystem What is RingCentral? RingCentral has been part of the business communications market since 1999, making it one of the oldest names among today's leading VoIP service providers . Over the years, the platform has grown far beyond internet calling. Today it combines voice, video meetings, SMS, fax, team messaging, AI powered meeting summaries, contact center capabilities, and hundreds of software integrations inside one unified workspace. Its biggest advantage is maturity. Thousands of businesses have built their communication stack around RingCentral over many years. Large organizations appreciate its extensive integration library, broad hardware compatibility, and worldwide coverage. Companies running Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft Teams, Zendesk, ServiceNow, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, and dozens of other business applications rarely struggle to connect them. For businesses comparing UCaaS platforms , RingCentral often appears near the top of every shortlist because it supports almost every communication workflow imaginable. At the same time, all those capabilities create a platform that can feel overwhelming for smaller outbound sales teams. Organizations with only a handful of SDRs may never use a large percentage of what RingCentral offers. That is where the buying decision becomes much more practical. If your company needs enterprise communications first, RingCentral deserves serious consideration. If your priority is outbound prospecting, AI coaching, and booking meetings faster, there may be better options later in this list. Why RingCentral Is a Good Alternative to 8x8 Companies comparing these two platforms usually arrive at the same conclusion. Both target medium and enterprise businesses, both offer broad communication capabilities, and both continue expanding their AI functionality. The differences become easier to see once you look at daily operations rather than feature checklists. Massive integration ecosystem Businesses rarely operate with one application anymore. Sales teams rely on CRM software, marketing automation, calendar platforms, customer support tools, document management systems, and analytics software every single day. RingCentral supports more than 500 native integrations, significantly more than 8x8. For organizations with an established software stack, this removes many of the compatibility concerns that appear during software migrations. Public pricing makes budgeting easier Many buyers dislike entering long sales conversations before learning subscription costs. RingCentral publishes pricing for its primary business phone plans, making budgeting considerably easier during procurement. 8x8 frequently requires speaking with its sales team before businesses receive complete pricing information for higher level subscriptions. Finance teams generally appreciate greater transparency early in the buying process. Better suited for everyday business communications Although both products include contact center software, RingCentral maintains a broader focus across general business communication. Voice calls, internal collaboration, meetings, messaging, and administration receive equal attention. 8x8 leans much more heavily toward larger contact center environments that manage inbound customer service operations. Companies wanting a complete business communication platform without making contact center workflows their primary focus often prefer RingCentral. Stable performance across multiple devices One area where RingCentral receives consistent praise is device continuity. Employees can begin conversations from a desktop application, continue from a mobile phone, and access the same conversations across multiple devices without losing context. Businesses with remote employees or hybrid work environments often value this consistency. Familiar enterprise experience Organizations already accustomed to enterprise software generally adapt to RingCentral fairly quickly. Its administrative controls, reporting options, permissions, and integrations provide plenty of room for larger operations to expand over time. Areas Worth Considering Before Switching RingCentral improves on several aspects of 8x8, although it shares a few characteristics that buyers should understand before making a decision. Customer support receives mixed feedback, particularly among smaller businesses that are not enterprise accounts. The platform contains hundreds of settings, meaning first time administrators should expect a learning curve during deployment. Unlimited calling also remains geographically limited, making international organizations evaluate their usage carefully before selecting a subscription. For businesses asking 8x8 vs RingCentral vs Dialpad: which is the best business phone system? , RingCentral remains one of the safest choices for companies needing reliability, broad integrations, and mature communications infrastructure. Sales organizations focused primarily on outbound prospecting, however, may benefit more from software designed around revenue generation rather than enterprise communications. RingCentral Pricing RingCentral keeps its primary pricing relatively straightforward. Core, $30 per user each month This entry plan includes unlimited domestic calling, business SMS, video meetings, and call recording. It provides the core communication features most organizations expect from a modern cloud business phone system . Advanced, $35 per user each month CRM integrations, advanced reporting, and more administrative capabilities become available at this level. Most sales organizations looking for deeper workflow automation begin with this subscription.
